final_candidates.decision_summary: Position 42 in the core activation domain shows 66% natural Gly frequency and maximal ESM-1v plausibility (1.0); Gly adds flexibility adjacent to the Cys-rich region without disrupting the ARM, a low-risk candidate for modulating transactivation.

H13R is the only N-terminal candidate with nonzero natural mutant frequency (~5.8%) and lies in the variable proline-rich region far from essential Cys-rich/ARM motifs; added positive charge could aid TAR/P-TEFb interactions.
K29Q shows modest evolutionary tolerance (~1.4%) and nonzero PLM plausibility at the variable Cys-rich/CORE boundary; charge loss is a mild concern but less risky than ARM-proximal alternatives.

stop_reason.detail: Available informative tools (MSA, PLM, annotation) have been applied and consistently rank A42G, H13R, K29Q; no tool measures transactivation directly, so extra rounds would not change the Top-3.

history.rationale: K28 acetylation enhances Tat-CycT1-TAR complex formation; glutamine mimics constitutive acetylation, potentially boosting P-TEFb recruitment and transactivation.
K28 is a regulatory Lys near the cysteine-rich activation region; acetyl-mimic Q is plausible but may interfere with reversible acetylation, so keep but slightly de-risk pending tools.
Both MSA (0% Q frequency) and ESM-1v (0.0001) strongly disfavor K28Q; demote below better-supported candidates.
K50 acetylation in the ARM promotes Tat release from TAR for elongation; K50Q mimics this acetylated state and may accelerate the transcription cycle.
K50 sits inside the essential ARM/TAR-binding basic stretch 49-57; neutralizing charge is likely to impair RNA binding and nuclear localization.

rejection.reason: K50 sits inside the essential ARM/TAR-binding basic stretch 49-57; neutralizing charge is likely to impair RNA binding and nuclear localization.

history.rationale: K51 acetylation is implicated in Tat turnover and cofactor exchange; acetyl-mimetic substitution may enhance processive transactivation.
K51 is also within the ARM/basic RNA-binding motif; Lys-to-Gln removes positive charge and is high-risk for transactivation loss.

rejection.reason: K51 is also within the ARM/basic RNA-binding motif; Lys-to-Gln removes positive charge and is high-risk for transactivation loss.

history.rationale: Adjacent to K28 in the cysteine-rich/core region; charge-neutralization may modulate P-TEFb binding affinity.
Adjacent to K28 in a Lys-rich regulatory patch, but charge-neutralizing changes here are less clearly tied to the core TAR/PTEFb interfaces; keep lower priority.
K29Q has modest evolutionary tolerance (1.4%) and low-but-nonzero PLM plausibility; position 29 lies in the variable Cys-rich/CORE boundary, though charge loss is a mild concern.
Proline-rich N-terminus is variable across clades; introducing basic residue may improve interaction with transcription machinery without disrupting core domains.
Early N-terminal substitution preserves positive charge while potentially modulating Tat folding/partner contacts; plausible but mechanistically indirect.

H13R is the only N-terminal candidate with nonzero natural mutant frequency (5.8%) and sits in the variable proline-rich region, far from the essential Cys-rich and ARM motifs; adding a positive charge could aid TAR/P-TEFb interactions.
Position 17 lies in a variable N-terminal segment outside essential domains; basic substitution may strengthen coactivator engagement.
Adds positive charge in the N-terminal acidic/proline-rich region without touching Cys core or ARM; could improve electrostatics but has uncertain phenotype linkage.
Q17R adds charge in a variable region but has zero natural frequency; kept as a backup only.
Position 20 precedes the Cys-rich domain; small hydrophobic substitution is likely tolerated and may stabilize folding of the activation domain.
Small conservative change near the N terminus may affect local flexibility/phosphorylation context, but is unlikely to be a dominant transactivation enhancer.
Weak MSA tolerance but near-zero PLM plausibility; low priority.
Conservative Lys-to-Arg change in the variable N-terminus preserves positive charge while altering H-bonding potential.
Charge-preserving Lys-to-Arg in the N-terminal region is viability-conservative and may alter ubiquitination/acetylation competition while retaining basic character.
Conservative Lys-to-Arg preserves positive charge and has the best PLM score among N-terminal candidates, despite zero observed natural frequency.
Core-region lysine involved in protein interactions; alanine scan-type substitution could relieve inhibitory contacts, though risk of function loss exists.
Alanine removes a basic residue between the cysteine-rich core and ARM; charge loss is risky for cofactor/RNA electrostatics, so demote.
Position 41 is highly conserved (entropy 0.515), A never observed in homologs, PLM score 0.0, and Lys-to-Ala removes charge right before the ARM; high risk of transactivation loss.

rejection.reason: Position 41 is highly conserved (entropy 0.515), A never observed in homologs, PLM score 0.0, and Lys-to-Ala removes charge right before the ARM; high risk of transactivation loss.

history.rationale: Small residue flexibility change in the core domain may fine-tune folding of the activation region essential for P-TEFb binding.
Glycine may increase local flexibility near the basic domain boundary, but effects are ambiguous and could destabilize the core-to-ARM transition.

A42G shows the strongest combined support: 66% natural G frequency at position 42 and maximal ESM-1v plausibility (1.0). Located in the core activation domain adjacent to the Cys-rich region, a Gly substitution likely adds flexibility without disrupting the zinc-finger or ARM, making it a low-risk candidate for modulating transactivation.
